paper_title: Open Problem: Model Selection for Contextual Bandits
authors: Dylan J. Foster, Akshay Krishnamurthy, Haipeng Luo

context: Stochastic Setting. The model selection problem for contextual bandits has yet to be solved even for the stochastic setting, and even when the model is well-specified. Here, we assume: (1) {(xt , `t )}Tt=1 are drawn i.i.d. from a fixed distribution D; (2) Each class Πm is induced by a class of regression functions Fm ⊂ (X × A → [0, 1]), in the sense that Πm = {πf ∣ f ∈ Fm }, where πf (x) ∶= argmina∈A f (x, a); (3) The problem is realizable/well-specified in the sense that there exists index m⋆ and regression function f⋆ ∈ Fm⋆ such that E[`(a) ∣ x] = f⋆ (x, a), for all x, a. The final version of our open problem asks for a model selection guarantee when the problem is stochastic and well-specified. Note that these assumptions imply that the optimal unconstrained policy (in terms of expected loss) is πf⋆ . As such, here we only ask for a regret bound against class Πm⋆ . From an algorithmic perspective, this is the easiest version of the problem. Open Problem 2 For some value α ∈ [1/2, 1), design an algorithm for contextual bandits that for any sequence F1 ⊂ F2 ⊂ ⋯FM = F, whenever data is stochastic and realizable, ensures T T E[∑ `t (at ) − ∑ `t (πf⋆ (xt ))] ≤ O(poly(K, M, log log∣F∣) ⋅ T α log1−α ∣Fm⋆ ∣).
